To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

teams are most likely to achieve their potential when team members are able to speak up with the knowledge and skills they have, and when they are able to influence the work of the team so that the team is able to do its best for the patient.

teams can be more intelligent than any of their members working individually, and that the best way to ensure that this happens is to ensure that team members speak up when they have relevant knowledge to share and that they have a way to influence the team to do its best for the patient, such as by having the team's leader solicit input from all team members before making decisions.

the most intelligent teams are those that (1) include members who have relevant knowledge, (2) encourage members to speak up when their expertise can be helpful, and (3) influence the team to do its collective best for patients.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can help teams achieve more than the sum of their parts.
how teams can maximize the intelligence that is available to them.
the question of what teams can do to ensure that they capitalize on the collective intelligence of the group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most effective teams have a diverse range of knowledge, skills and abilities, and they use these to their fullest potential.
the team's ability to capitalize on the collective intelligence of its members depends on how well the team communicates, both in terms of who speaks up and who is listened to.
teamwork in health care requires the inclusion of all team members, and the communication of their ideas, in order to achieve collective intelligence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective teams are those that are inclusive of the expertise of their members, but that are also open to new ideas and information from those members.
teams can only be as good as their members, and that members are only as good as the way they interact with one another.
the most important thing is for team members to be able to speak up when they have relevant knowledge, but to do so in a way that is not disruptive to the team.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the best way to maximize collective intelligence is to create an environment in which team members feel comfortable sharing their knowledge and opinions and are encouraged to influence the team's decisions.

the most effective teams are those that leverage their members' unique knowledge, skills, abilities, and experiences in ways that are inclusive, collaborative, and open. (PsycINFO Database Record (c) 2019 APA, all rights reserved)
